To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
phosphorylation of synap-sins at a specific site regulates neurite out growth.
the phosphorylation of a specific amino acid residue of synapsin, a synaptic vesicle protein, is required for the promotion of neurite outgrowth.
cAMP/PKA–mediated stimulation of neurite outgrowth is mediated, in part, by the phosphorylation at one amino acid residue in synapsins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of neurite outgrowth and regeneration.
the mechanisms by which the nervous system develops, functions, and is maintained.
the role of the synapsin family of synaptic proteins in neurite outgrowth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cAMP promotes neurite out growth by phosphorylating synapsins on a particular site, which is required for neurite out growth.
PKA-dependent neurite outgrowth requires the phosphorylation of the synapsins at one specific site, and the dephosphorylation of the synapses at the same site.
the PKA-mediated phosphorylation of synapses at a single site, S-62, is a critical event for neurite outgrowth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
synapsin phosphorylation at serine 66 is a molecular switch that can be used to control neurite outgrowth.
the phosphorylation of one amino acid in a synapsin isoform regulates neurite out growth.
synapsin phosphorylation by protein kinase A is required for neurite outgrowth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synapsin protein kinase A–mediated switch regulates neurite out growth.
the phosphorylation of a single residue in synapsins, which is regulated by cAMP/PKA, controls neurite outgrowth.
synapsin is an important mediator of cAMP/PK A–stimulated neuritogenesis.
